findings.page: PDF p. 38 (printed 14) and PDF p. 60 (printed 36); convention stated at PDF p. 20 (printed xvi)
findings.evidence: PDF p. 38 (Ch. 1, §1.5, Common Mistakes): "code, numerics, and non-Latin scripts can run 2–5× the naive word-count estimate (rule of thumb; the multiplier is tokenizer- and language-specific) [ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark][HYPOTHESIS]". PDF p. 60 (Ch. 2, §2.5): "actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark][HYPOTHESIS][UNMEASURED]". The Preface's label rules (PDF p. 20) state: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; the two tags are set with no space between them and never break across a line", and the Axis-1 vocabulary is the closed set "[1P] / [canonical scenario] / [ILLUSTRATIVE] / [2°] / [LAB]".
findings.issue: Two occurrences embed free prose inside the provenance tag ("[ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark]"), which is not a member of the book's own closed Axis-1 vocabulary and breaks the mandatory one-tag-per-axis, no-space, no-inline-text pair format. The qualifier belongs in the surrounding prose, not inside the brackets. The defect is not cosmetic for this book: the Preface's whole verification scheme depends on labels being machine-parseable tokens, and the second occurrence also stacks a third bracket ([UNMEASURED]) onto a pair, which the Preface permits only as a third axis 'riding along' rather than appended as free text.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace both with the bare tag pair and move the qualifier into the prose immediately before it — e.g. "an industry rule of thumb, with no named survey or benchmark [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]" — and re-check the whole document for any other occurrence of a bracketed tag containing a colon or free text (search for "[ILLUSTRATIVE:" and "[1P:").

findings.page: PDF p. 27 (printed 3) and PDF p. 78 (printed 68); convention stated at PDF p. 23 (printed xix)
findings.chapter: Ch. 1 §1.1.2, Ch. 4 (Canonical Workload box) — Appendix A cross-references
findings.evidence: PDF p. 27 (Ch. 1, §1.1.2): "the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next card states a native 262K-token window with YaRN extension to 1M, and the GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M [1P][FACT] model cards: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; HF zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash; DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10". PDF p. 78 (Ch. 4, Canonical Workload box): "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios) is its deliberate relaxation, not a correction". The Preface's cross-reference convention (PDF p. 23) states: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N."
findings.issue: Both Appendix A references violate the book's own stated appendix-numbering convention: "§10" carries no letter suffix (the convention's example is "9A"), and "§A.7" uses a letter prefix, which is the figure-numbering form (A.N) rather than the section form (N-letter). "§A.7" additionally points at "Fig A.2", so a reader following the section pointer lands on a differently numbered figure, and neither form matches the "9A" pattern used elsewhere in the book ("Appendix A §9A", cited on PDF pp. 46, 66, 79). At least one of the two forms cannot resolve to the appendix's actual section labels.
findings.fix_instruction: Check the actual section labels in Appendix A and rewrite both pointers in the sanctioned form — e.g. "Appendix A §10A" and "Appendix A §7A" — and add "§ 10A" / "§ 7A" style consistency to the appendix's own Contents listing so the labels are discoverable. Sweep the full document for the patterns "Appendix A §", "Appendix A's §" and any bare "§A." to catch the remaining instances.

findings.chapter: Appendix A reference style (Ch 1 §1.1.2, Preface evidence-cutoff section, Ch 4 Table 4-2 box)
findings.evidence: Preface (p.19): "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N." But: p.7 "...all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10)"; p.21 "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe" and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)"; p.102 "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios)".
findings.issue: Internal inconsistency in Appendix A section-reference style: the stated convention is letter-suffixed section labels (§9A) with A.N reserved for figures, yet the book references appendix sections as '§10' (no letter suffix, p.7) and as 'A.6'/'A.3'/'§A.7' (figure-style labels used for sections, pp. 21, 102). A reader cannot tell whether 'A.6' denotes section 6, section 6A, or figure A.6 (which also exists per the List of Figures).
findings.fix_instruction: Pick one appendix section-label scheme and enforce it: either relabel all section refs to the letter-suffixed form (§10A, §6A, §3A, §7A) or amend the Preface convention sentence to describe the actual mixed scheme, and rename figure refs to an unambiguous form (e.g., 'Fig A.2') wherever collision is possible. Verify against the appendix's own headings (pp. 482–514).
